name: LassoNet
summary: For 3D point clouds on a desktop screen, the user draws a lasso with the mouse and a deep neural network infers which points they meant, using the lasso and the current viewpoint, so occluded regions can be selected without rotating the view.
howItWorks: The user draws a lasso on the 2D view of a point cloud. Points are moved into the camera's coordinate frame, a naive frustum selection finds candidates, an intention filter and farthest-point sampling reduce them, and a hierarchical point network trained on over 30,000 lasso-selection records predicts the intended subset. Selections can be combined with union, intersection and subtraction. In a user study it was compared with CylinderSelection and SpaceCast and improved selection effectiveness and efficiency across point clouds, viewpoints and lasso sizes.
advantages: Learns the user's intent rather than relying on hand-crafted density heuristics.
Can select occluded clusters without changing the viewpoint.
limitations: Needs a large set of training selections; limited to mouse lassos on a 2D display.

relationships.note: Earlier density-based lasso selection for point clouds.
